plan.summary: This 4-week block is a simple off-camp build for a beginner boxer with one 30-minute S&C session per week and bodyweight-only equipment. Week 1 establishes a baseline on the main lower-body strength pattern with a safe multi-rep assessment, then Weeks 2-4 build general force, power, trunk strength, and a small dose of safe neck work. The wider 12-week cycle keeps building through Week 8, then shifts toward sharper speed and power expression in Weeks 9-12 without forcing a fight-camp peak.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic lower-body strength, simple power, trunk stiffness, and safe foundational work with recoverable fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the same key patterns with slightly harder variations and tighter quality control while keeping fatigue manageable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and express it with faster, sharper jumping and boxing-supportive power outputs.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a soft landing. Reset between reps and stop if height drops off.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement jump feels uncoordinated. Start from a still quarter squat and jump fast.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jumps
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is limited or impact tolerance is low. Keep contacts light and springy.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a controlled warm-up, then build to one hard set per side with clean form. Log the reps achieved on the harder side to set your starting point for the next weeks.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your hardest clean set of 3-5 reps per side using a tempo or range that makes the set challenging. Log the reps and variation used so the app can track your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Beat the quality of this top set next time with better control, range, or reps before moving to a harder variation.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if a regular split squat is too easy. Keep the front foot planted and torso steady.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squat setup is uncomfortable. Step back under control and drive up through the front leg.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a variation that leaves 1-2 clean reps in reserve. Keep the body straight and move with full control.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, table, or sturdy surface if floor push-ups are too hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lower if regular push-ups are too easy with bodyweight only.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Stay long from head to heel and do not let the hips sag.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if side planks are too difficult to hold cleanly.

exercises.name: Supine Neck Isometric Hold
exercises.notes: Lie on your back and gently press the head into the floor without straining. Keep the effort smooth and submaximal.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Towel Neck Flexion Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a towel for light hand resistance if floor setup is awkward. Keep the effort easy and pain-free.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump fast and land quietly. Take enough rest so every rep stays crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a simpler jump pattern. Pause briefly in the start position before takeoff.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jumps
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if impact tolerance is low. Keep the rhythm elastic and light.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use the variation from Week 1 that was challenging but clean. Control the bottom and drive up hard.

performanceTarget.prompt: Aim to improve one set with more reps, better depth, or a harder variation while keeping form solid.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the base version is too easy. Keep the front leg doing the work.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you move better with a stepping pattern. Keep balance steady.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Stop before the hips sag or the neck reaches forward. Use a harder or easier variation to stay in the target range.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard floor reps are not yet clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard reps are too easy. Lower for 3 seconds and press up hard.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Drive through the heel and pause briefly at the top without arching the lower back.

substitutionOptions.name: Two-Leg Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if single-leg control is not there yet.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep the ribs down and lower back gently pressed toward the floor. Shorten the lever if needed.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow hold cannot be maintained cleanly.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Neck Isometric Hold
exercises.notes: Gently press the side of the head into the floor or your hand. Keep the effort controlled and pain-free.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Hand-Resisted Lateral Neck Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use light hand pressure only. Do not strain or hold your breath.

exercises.name: Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Start from a still quarter squat and explode up. Land soft and reset each rep.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the paused start feels awkward. Still prioritize jump height and landing control.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jumps
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if impact needs to stay very low.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use this only if your regular split squat is now clearly too easy. Stay balanced and keep the front knee tracking well.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best clean set per side and improve control or reps before adding more difficulty.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the rear-foot-elevated version is too unstable or too hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if setup space is limited.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Press fast on the way up while keeping the body rigid. Use the variation that keeps all reps clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if full push-ups still break down.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if regular reps are too easy.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Step back quietly, stay tall, and drive through the front leg.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if balance is better in a stationary stance.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Keep the top hip stacked and the trunk braced the whole time.

substitutionOptions.name: Hollow Body Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if shoulder support is uncomfortable in the side plank.

exercises.name: Prone Neck Isometric Hold
exercises.notes: Lie face down and gently press the forehead into a folded towel or your hands. Keep the neck long and do not strain.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Hand-Resisted Neck Extension Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use very light pressure and keep the effort smooth.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Keep every rep snappy and stop while you still feel springy.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you prefer the simpler paused start.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jumps
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if legs feel beaten up and you need a lighter option.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use the same variation as last week but leave extra reps in the tank. Smooth reps only.

performanceTarget.prompt: Use this week to move cleanly and finish fresh rather than chasing fatigue.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if it is already stable and comfortable.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if your hips or knees prefer the stepping pattern.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Keep the reps smooth and leave a little in reserve. No grinders this week.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need cleaner reps with less effort.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if regular reps are still too easy without adding fatigue.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Pause briefly at the top and keep the pelvis level.

substitutionOptions.name: Two-Leg Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the single-leg version causes cramping or poor control.
